title: Polar-furrow arrangements follow relative cell sizes, not species identity

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Polar-furrow arrangements follow relative cell sizes, not species identity

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Small changes in the relative sizes of the four cells carry the median partition and its polar furrows through all their possible arrangements, which correspond to those observed in various embryos; these arrangements are physical phenomena distributed without relation to zoological classification, not species characters.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: So, by slight and delicate modifications in the relative size of the cells, we may pass through all the possible arrangements of the median partition, and of the “furrows” which correspond to its upper and lower edges; and every one of these arrangements has been frequently observed in the four-celled stage of various embryos.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “Polar furrow variants and cell size”. Scope: four-celled stage of embryos across molluscs, annelids, coelenterates, vertebrates and others

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cell volumes, furrow arrangement, and taxonomic identity support a direct comparative model. Current open data cover several model species but not the wide phylogenetic scope asserted, and species-level confounding remains.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across four-cell embryos, model polar-furrow topology from relative blastomere volumes and test whether size predicts arrangement better than species identity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Lineage-specific adhesion and cleavage programs covary with species.

Cross-phyla image protocols and stage definitions differ.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Relative cell size versus furrow topology is a well-posed comparison, and it can be started on frog and sea-urchin volumes. The claim's scope is a cross-phylum distribution, and most of that comparative sample is still in uncompiled embryological plates. Phylogenetic non-independence of egg size is a real but manageable confound for the subset that is digitized.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: At the four-cell stage, predict polar-furrow arrangement from relative blastomere volumes and compare that prediction with a model that assigns arrangements by clade. Arrangements tracking size ratios, with little phylogenetic signal once size is controlled, would support the claim; clade-conserved furrows at the same size ratios would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Related species often share egg proportions, so size and classification are not fully independent.

Molluscs, annelids and coelenterates, where many of the classical furrow variants were drawn, are poorly represented in these databases.
